name: Cadrex – Chaska (Previously Richlind Metal Fabricators LLC)
old_description: Quality and Precision: Why Quality Assurance is Important in Precision Machining
about:
Cadrex Chaska operates in Chaska, Minnesota The facility traces its roots to 1963 when Richlind Metal Fabricators was founded as a precision metal fabrication shop. In January 2022, Richlind was acquired by Cadrex Manufacturing Solutions and began operating as a Cadrex company later that year, formally transitioning to the Cadrex brand.

The site provides precision fabrication of finished components and complex assemblies. Core processes include shearing, sawing, laser cutting, turning, forming, and CNC machining, supplemented by welding, plastic injection molding, mechanical assembly, painting and finishing, and system integration and testing. As part of the Cadrex network, the facility draws on a combined 1.5 million square feet of capacity, over 600 machines, and 20 locations across the U.S. and Mexico, with dedicated prototyping, design-for-manufacturability, tool design, and custom automation programs.

The Chaska facility serves aerospace and defense, medical (holding ISO 13485 certification), data center infrastructure, commercial, and broader industrial markets. Through the Cadrex portfolio, customers also include information communication technology, warehouse automation and robotics, kiosk and gaming, and renewable energy and electrical infrastructure sectors.

Richlind was established to deliver progressive technology in metals and plastics fabrication with engineering support and prototype-to-production processing. The acquisition by Cadrex expanded capacity, capabilities, and expertise, reinforcing a commitment to outstanding quality and value for the industries served.

name: Cal-Maine Farm
old_description: In 1996, Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. became a public company trading on NASDAQ under ticker “CALM”. The Company has demonstrated a long history of impressive profitable growth and operational excellence, reaching a milestone of selling over one billion dozen eggs for the first time in 2014. In addition to organic growth, we have expanded our operations and production capacity through a disciplined acquisition strategy, successfully integrating 26 companies since 1989. We achieved sales of over $2.9 billion with over 1.2 billion dozens sold in fiscal 2026.
about:
Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. was founded in 1957 by Fred R. Adams, Jr. in Jackson, Mississippi. The company is headquartered in Ridgeland, Mississippi, and has been publicly traded on NASDAQ under the ticker CALM since 1996. It began as a single egg operation and grew through a series of mergers and acquisitions, including the 1969 merger of Adams Foods with Dairy Fresh Products and Maine Egg Farms to form Cal-Maine Foods.

The company produces a full range of egg products, from conventional and cage-free shell eggs to organic, free-range, pasture-raised, and nutritionally enhanced specialty eggs, as well as prepared egg-based foods such as ready-to-eat egg products and breakfast foods. As of May 2026, its operations comprised 2 breeding facilities, 2 hatcheries, 29 feed mills, 51 shell egg production facilities, 38 pullet growing facilities, 52 processing and packaging facilities, and 5 food manufacturing facilities across multiple states. The company maintains approximately 50 million laying hens and sold 1.2 billion dozen eggs in fiscal 2026, generating $2.9 billion in net sales.

Cal-Maine Foods serves retail and foodservice channels nationwide under brands including Eggland's Best, Land O' Lakes, Farmhouse Eggs, Crepini, and Van's Foods. Its customers range from household consumers to foodservice operators and retail chains across the United States.

The company states its purpose is to be the consumer-driven provider of nutritious, affordable, and sustainable eggs and egg-based foods that fit today's lifestyles. It emphasizes a disciplined acquisition strategy — integrating 26 companies since 1989 — and commitments to sustainable operations, strong corporate governance, and community support.

name: California Fine Wire Co.
old_description: , allowing us to support highly regulated medical, aerospace, defense, and industrial markets. Since 1961, CFW has engineered wire solutions that meet exacting performance quality standards.
about:
California Fine Wire Co. was founded in June 1961 in Grover Beach, California, when Michael A. Greenelsh started the business with a single wire drawing machine. Over six decades, the company has grown into a multi‑million‑dollar operation supplying specialty wire and ribbon worldwide.

The company manufactures and processes fine and ultra‑fine wire in round and flat profiles, with diameters ranging from 0.0004″ to 0.125″. Core processes include precision drawing, enamel coating (insulating), PTFE and ceramic coating, electroplating, flat‑ribbon rolling, annealing, stranding and twisting, cutting, straightening, and spooling. CFW operates 25 enamel coating machines and maintains an in‑house testing laboratory capable of dimensional measurements to 0.00001″ resolution.

CFW serves highly regulated markets including medical, aerospace, defense, electronics, semiconductor, industrial, and research sectors. Its products are used in implanted cardiac devices, drift chambers, semiconductor interconnects, wire‑bonding assemblies, medical devices, aerospace systems, and high‑temperature industrial sensors. The company works with a broad alloy palette—aluminum, copper, gold, nickel, platinum, refractory metals, stainless steel, thermocouple alloys, and composite‑clad conductors.

Founder Michael A. Greenelsh once said the company’s real specialty is fulfilling customers’ specific needs, a philosophy that has guided CFW for over 60 years. The firm emphasizes tight tolerances, traceable raw materials from approved vendors, and a quality system certified to ISO 9001 with ITAR registration for defense work.

name: Capital Electro Circuits Inc
old_description: exceptional craftsmanship, on-time delivery, and customer-focused solutions
about:
Capital Electro Circuits Inc., based in Gaithersburg, Maryland, has been manufacturing printed circuit boards since 1985. The independently owned company is led by General Manager Raj Jagani and operates a domestic fabrication facility focused on rigid and flexible PCB technologies.

The shop produces rigid, flexible, and rigid‑flex boards with capabilities that include multilayer constructions up to 16 layers, finished thicknesses up to 1.300 inches, copper weights up to 6 oz outer/4 oz inner, and advanced features such as blind/buried vias, edge plating, and castellations. Materials span standard FR‑4 and high‑Tg laminates, polyimides, and a wide range of RF/microwave substrates from Rogers, Arlon, Taconic, and TMM/Teflon families. In‑house services cover CAM with DFM analysis, CNC routing and milling, electrical testing, and a full suite of surface finishes including HASL, ENIG, ENEPIG, immersion tin/silver, and hard gold.

The company serves aerospace and defense (supplying 100 % U.S.-made boards for military and avionics programs), medical and healthcare (precision boards for imaging and diagnostic equipment), telecommunications (high‑frequency circuits for 5G and satellite), automotive and EV (durable boards for electric and autonomous vehicles), and RF/microwave applications. Named customers include Northrop Grumman, BAE Systems, NASA, Lockheed Martin, Honeywell, Sandia National Laboratories, Booz Allen Hamilton, and the U.S. Army.

Capital Electro Circuits positions itself as a specialty fabricator that takes on jobs outside standard PCB lines, often developing custom processes for unique designs. Its stated mission is to support what the customer requires, not only what they ask for, and it maintains a conflict‑minerals sourcing policy with vetted vendors and full CMRT disclosure.

name: Capitol Iron Works
old_description: Based in Rockville, Maryland, Capitol Iron Works specializes in custom ornamental metalwork projects based on unique design ideas, working with ferrous and nonferrous metals, such as stainless steel, aluminum and bronze. The company also works with structural steel and glass. Some of the most common projects include fabrication and installation of architectural railings, stairs, handrails, glass and cable railings, steel fencing, balconies, canopies and automatic gates.
about:
Capitol Iron Works operates from Gaithersburg, Maryland, in the heart of the DC–Maryland–Virginia corridor. The company was founded in August 2014 by Ronald Vargas, who immigrated from Nicaragua in 2004 and learned welding as a helper at Bethesda Iron Works before earning his certification and launching his own shop, initially called Capitol Iron Solutions. Vargas serves as president and co‑owner.

The shop produces custom ornamental and architectural metalwork in ferrous and non‑ferrous metals — stainless steel, aluminum, bronze, structural steel, wrought iron, and glass. Core processes include welding, cutting, shaping, decorative detailing, powder‑coat finishing, and on‑site installation. The facility has expanded from a 1,100‑square‑foot space with a single fabrication bay to a 4,300‑square‑foot plant housing three fabrication units, staffed by 14 employees. Project sizes range from $1,000 residential railings to $500,000 commercial installations, with 2018 revenue projected at $1.5 million.

Capitol Iron Works serves residential, commercial, and government clients across the DMV. Notable government work includes bronze railing fabrication and installation for the Architect of the Capitol at the Rayburn House Office Building. The company also works with architects, contractors, and property owners in cities such as Bethesda, Rockville, Alexandria, and Arlington.

Vargas attributes the firm’s rapid growth to two factors: a loyal, low‑turnover team (only one departure in four years) and a willingness to tackle technically difficult, intricate projects that other shops decline. He emphasizes on‑schedule delivery, direct communication, and a single‑source approach from design through installation.

name: Capsule Technologies
old_description: Philips Capsule is now part of the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio of solutions – a comprehensive, clinically focused ecosystem designed to enhance care delivery across the healthcare enterprise, with a goal of improving patient outcomes and reducing clinician burnout.
about:
Capsule Technologies, now operating as Philips Capsule within the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio, is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company was acquired by Philips and integrated into its acute care informatics division; its founding year and original founders are not disclosed in public materials.

The company develops vendor‑neutral medical device integration and clinical informatics software. Its platform captures live‑streaming data from over 1,200 medical devices and delivers it to more than 100 downstream systems, including electronic health records, alarm management, and research databases. The portfolio spans medical device integration (Philips Axon, Capsule Neuron, Capsule Vitals Stream, Chart Xpress), a medical device information platform, virtual care management (eCareManager), retrospective analytics (Clinical Insights Manager), clinical surveillance (Capsule Surveillance), and a critical care clinical information system (IntelliSpace Critical Care and Anesthesia).

Customers are hospitals and health systems worldwide. Named references include Hamilton Health Sciences in Canada, CoxHealth in the United States, and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in the United Kingdom. The solutions target acute care, perioperative, and virtual care environments.

The company emphasizes a vendor‑neutral, open ecosystem that works with existing infrastructure, deep clinical and operational experience to fit workflows, and a track record of measurable outcomes such as time savings and a seven‑year run of positive Net Promoter Scores.

about:
Captor Corporation was established in 1965 in Tipp City, Ohio, by an engineering-oriented management team that included several experienced veterans. The company built a dedicated manufacturing facility shortly after inception, which has since expanded to a 35,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art plant housing engineering, sales, and production under one roof.

The company designs and manufactures custom EMI filters, capacitors, inductors, coils, cable assemblies, wire harnesses, electromechanical assemblies, and power distribution units. Its in-house capabilities span engineering, custom capacitor winding, coil winding (toroid, bobbin-wound, tube-wound, C-core), cable and harness fabrication, box-build assembly, and environmental testing including altitude, humidity, thermal shock, vibration, and hermetic seal. Captor has produced over 10,000 custom filter designs and focuses on low- to medium-volume production.

Captor serves OEMs in aerospace, defense, military communications, secure communications (including SCIF and TEMPEST applications), medical equipment, telecommunications, radar systems, and missile launching systems.

The company positions itself as a leader in custom EMI filters, stating that its custom solutions are often delivered faster and at lower cost than competitors' off-the-shelf parts, with no added cost for customization. Its mission emphasizes highest-quality EMI filters, customer listening, a safe workplace, continuous improvement, and total customer satisfaction.
